title: Sign-in
observed: The initial Railway sign-in surface was captured before the user signed in on wercomfg.app.
assessment: Clear sign-in entry point. Current-source review finds the recovery button has no action; this was not exercised after authentication.
recommendation: Implement real account recovery and preserve the requested destination through sign-in.
limit: No password reset, session expiry, or alternate role sign-in tested.

title: Action Inbox
observed: The inbox presents urgent issue categories and affected-item counts.
assessment: Useful consolidation of exceptions. Generic Open actions lose the affected-record scope; setup completion and operational blockers need distinct explanations.
recommendation: Open a filtered affected-record queue with an explicit count, owner and next action.
limit: Counts are a point-in-time sample; no blockers were changed.

title: Dashboard
observed: Ten similarly weighted metrics and a large machine-capacity section occupy the overview.
assessment: Broad operational visibility, but the screen requires scanning many equally prominent cards. An overdue count of 7 does not carry its scope into the destination.
recommendation: Lead with exceptions and actionable queues, then supporting capacity and trends. Label period, filters and freshness.
limit: No latency or failure injection performed in production.

title: Overdue → work orders
observed: Clicking the overdue dashboard link opens the work-order list in All Active with Hide COTS selected; this list shows overdue 1.
assessment: Existing filters and table controls are useful. The count and destination scope are hard to reconcile, and long identifiers wrap repeatedly.
recommendation: Pass the actual overdue predicate into the URL; show inherited filter chips and count scope. Give identifiers more room.
limit: The audit does not establish which count is mathematically correct; filters differ.

title: Work-order detail
observed: The detail header has nine metric cards with truncated labels. Sample quantity completion is 1/1 while operation progress is 1/4.
assessment: Rich job context exists. Completion measures and the strong Complete action need a clearer relationship.
recommendation: Lead with next operation, blockers, due date and readiness. Explain quantity completion versus operation completion and any authorized override.
limit: Completion was not activated; the sample may reflect an intentional admin workflow.

title: Work-order secondary panels
observed: Large empty drawing/upload/preview and supporting panels precede the routing work farther down the page.
assessment: Documents and blocker reporting belong in job context, but empty optional panels consume task space.
recommendation: Collapse empty/supporting panels and surface current operation first. Replace implementation-oriented material/backflush prose with operator-facing consequences.
limit: This image shows secondary panels, not the operations table.

title: Scheduling
observed: The initial view expands capacity for 24 machines before the main planning work; the shown Aug 31–Sep 5 window excludes the current Sunday.
assessment: Capacity can be collapsed. Selection and mutation issues identified in source are described separately.
recommendation: Default to relevant machines and a useful planning window; preserve a compact capacity toggle and visible queue.
limit: No jobs selected for a bulk action or rescheduled.

title: Dispatch Board
observed: The board hides 22 idle machines and shows two active machine columns with 10 jobs.
assessment: Strong focus on machines with work, keyboard equivalents and material/changeover context. Source shows no automatic cross-station refresh.
recommendation: Add truthful updated-at state and safe reconciliation; expose due dates, remaining duration and job-detail links where useful.
limit: No reordering or cross-session mutation tested.

title: Time Clock initial selection
observed: The initial machine selection has an empty queue while work exists on other machines.
assessment: Machine choice is explicit, but 24 buttons do not reveal where the work is.
recommendation: Remember the station or user preference; show queue counts and relevant/favorite machines.
limit: Initial selection observed in this session only; do not infer every user gets the same default.

title: Time Clock populated queue
observed: Selecting Fit Up Station #1 reveals six jobs and an Up Next strip.
assessment: The queue supports direct production work. The top strip repeats jobs without enough operation context.
recommendation: Prioritize current operation and start/hold/complete context; include operation names in previews.
limit: No timers started or stopped.

title: Time Clock at 390 px
observed: Machine buttons fill the first screen. DOM measurement puts Up Next near y=972 and Job Queue near y=1252.
assessment: Mobile bottom navigation exists. The actual task is more than a screen below machine selection.
recommendation: Use a compact searchable station picker with queue counts; keep active job/next job in the first viewport.
limit: 390×844 browser viewport, not physical-device or glove testing.

title: Work orders at 390 px
observed: New WO extends to x≈414.7 in a 390 px viewport. Header and filters push the first job card down to about y=710.
assessment: Mobile cards already exist. The primary create action clips beyond the viewport.
recommendation: Wrap the primary action or give it its own row; move secondary actions into overflow and collapse optional filters.
limit: Measured one narrow viewport; 320 px and larger-device sweeps remain acceptance work.

title: New work order: part picker
observed: The form provides a searchable part picker with part type/revision metadata.
assessment: A useful entity selector. Optional serial information occupies substantial space before routing review.
recommendation: Group essential planning inputs first; reveal traceability fields when applicable and provide a compact review summary.
limit: No work order submitted.

title: New work order: selected part
observed: Part selection loads customer/routing context and an existing-open-work-order warning. Create was visible during routing loading.
assessment: Reuse of master data saves typing. Readiness needs an explicit current/loading/failed state; source confirms request-order risk.
recommendation: Tie preview and submit eligibility to the current part request. Keep the selected routing and deviations visible in final review.
limit: Cancel triggered a browser-tool/native-dialog stall; user reload restored access. No app-freeze conclusion or create outcome is claimed.

title: Warehouse receiving
observed: Nested Warehouse/Receiving tabs, summary cards and a long PO list leave a large empty detail region in the first viewport.
assessment: PO-based receiving is a sensible starting point. The selection prompt is displaced by the long list.
recommendation: Keep the prompt at the top of the detail panel and add quick PO/vendor lookup plus expected/overdue filters.
limit: No receipts or inspections recorded.

title: Receiving → Inspection Queue
observed: Clicking Inspection Queue changes the URL to /warehouse?tab=queue and renders Inventory.
assessment: The wrong module opens. Current source confirms the outer Warehouse tab and inner Receiving tab use the same query key.
recommendation: Use distinct URL state, such as tab=receiving&receivingTab=queue, and test refresh/Back/deep links.
limit: Browser-confirmed read-only navigation defect.

title: Shipping
observed: Ready to Ship shows 43 rows with repeated Schedule Shipment actions and little visible narrowing support.
assessment: Status queues are useful. Similar part rows need unit/WO identity, remaining quantity and useful date/customer filters.
recommendation: Add fulfillment context and a searchable queue; clarify Manual versus schedule-from-WO. Preserve partial-shipment remainder until fulfilled.
limit: Partial-shipment failure is source-traced, not executed live.

title: Purchasing
observed: The title says Purchasing & Receiving although receiving is elsewhere. Open POs shows 54 while the table includes received records. The Deleted segment is cramped.
assessment: PO statuses and vendor context are visible. The current Open POs value is the whole loaded list length.
recommendation: Correct summary scope and terminology, give filters adequate space, format currency consistently, and make row click open PO detail.
limit: Source verifies list-length count and print-focused row interaction; no print or vendor message triggered.

title: New PO dialog
observed: The clean dialog opens with vendor selection, date, line items and notes.
assessment: A coherent contained form. The native vendor list has many options, making known-vendor lookup slower.
recommendation: Use the established searchable entity picker; validate at the field/line and keep submit progress in the dialog.
limit: Opened and dismissed without entering or saving a PO.

title: MRP empty state
observed: No runs exist; the first metric says Run undefined while cards show zeros.
assessment: The main empty state explains how to begin, but undefined and pre-run zeros imply an analysis that has not occurred.
recommendation: Show Not analyzed until a run succeeds; remove redundant empty panels. Make action resolution describe actual supply creation or manual follow-up.
limit: MRP was not run; Process behavior and run races are source-only.

title: Quality management
observed: NCR/CAR/FAI navigation and summary filters are present. The sampled void NCR still offers Void and pending disposition.
assessment: Shared table and status filters exist. NCR/CAR lifecycle detail remains missing in current source; the void row needs terminal-state treatment.
recommendation: Provide review, disposition, owner, evidence and closure flows; disable irrelevant terminal actions and paginate the server dataset.
limit: Sample contains a pre-existing test record. No record was voided or edited; FAI has more complete detail behavior.

title: Traceability no-match search
observed: Submitting AUDIT-NO-MATCH-20260906 leaves only the search field and Trace button with no result or no-match message.
assessment: The lookup supports several useful identifiers. Silence gives no confirmation that the search completed.
recommendation: Distinguish initial/searching/no match/error states; offer query guidance and linked related records. Dispatch serial matches to serial tracing.
limit: No-match behavior observed; serial endpoint mismatch is source-only.

title: Quotes list
observed: The table shows two saved quotes, dates, line counts and a Send to Customer icon for the draft.
assessment: The summary is compact. History/status search is missing and send wording overstates the verified status-only endpoint.
recommendation: Provide Open/Converted/Expired views and truthful send/delivery states. Review the exact recipient/document only if sending is implemented.
limit: No customer message was sent or quote status changed.

title: Selected quote
observed: Selecting a 13-line quote opens a summary with number, customer and total; the lines remain inaccessible here.
assessment: Selection is reflected visibly, but the next review step is absent.
recommendation: Open a full detail page with lines, terms, revision history and draft edits; preview line-to-WO conversion explicitly.
limit: Browser-confirmed summary limitation. Conversion defects are source-only.

title: Documents
observed: The library has search/type filtering and 203 records, with Download and Delete row actions.
assessment: Catalog search and pagination are useful. Reviewing documents requires download and revisions lack a visible navigation flow.
recommendation: Add in-app preview, linked part/revision history and current/superseded status. Keep destructive actions secondary.
limit: No files downloaded, uploaded or deleted; no document contents audited.

title: Reports dashboard
observed: The screen combines period-based metrics, a separately labelled 14-day chart, 90-day vendor data, and machine utilization.
assessment: Individual panel windows are labelled. Utilization at 133.2% needs its denominator/meaning explained; chart labels are crowded.
recommendation: Expose metric definitions, consistent number formatting and accessible chart values; persist tab/period in URLs and make all employee entries reachable.
limit: No financial accuracy conclusion. Employee entry truncation and history-state behavior are source-traced.

title: Parts catalog
observed: Search, filters, saved filters, table/grid options and component visibility are available.
assessment: The hidden-component explanation is helpful. Dark blue identifiers and heavily wrapped part numbers impede scanning.
recommendation: Use a brighter dark-surface link token and allocate identifier width; preserve the existing catalog controls.
limit: No part edited. Screenshot rendering softness is not treated as a product defect.

title: Part BOM: Single Level
observed: Released Rev A has one item: WERCO-001-01, quantity 1 each.
assessment: Part identity, release state, revision and quantity are visible together.
recommendation: Preserve this context in all BOM views and support controlled draft-item editing.
limit: Read-only inspection of an existing test part.

title: Part BOM: Multi-Level
observed: Switching the same BOM to Multi-Level shows No items to display while its header still says 1 item.
assessment: This contradicts the prior view. Source confirms the response object is stored where the UI expects its items array.
recommendation: Use a typed explode response and display its items; distinguish failed reads from valid empty results.
limit: Browser-confirmed; no BOM changed or unreleased.

title: Visitor dialog Purpose picker
observed: Purpose is expanded and the DOM contains six options, but the options render behind the Add visit modal. Escape closes the full dialog.
assessment: The dialog has a name and clear time context. The required picker cannot be visually used as intended.
recommendation: Share overlay layers across Modal/SelectField/ComboBox; close the topmost popup first and retain form focus.
limit: Opened clean and dismissed; no visitor record created. Other SelectField-in-modal callers need regression coverage.
